evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Drive standardization, governance, and best practices for analytics development across the enterprise
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Strong governance/standardization/quality signals (data quality, governance, standards, scalable/repeatable/secure) are balanced against one explicit velocity phrase ("fast-paced environment"), giving parity rather than a clear rigour dominance.
evidence.domain_risk: Ensure data quality and governance in reporting environments, establishing standards for data visualization best practices and consistency
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: This is enterprise BI/reporting for an industrial manufacturer with no financial, regulatory, or safety-critical language — errors affect business decision quality, not compliance or public-facing risk.
evidence.collaboration_width: Analytics Engineers; Data Engineers; AI/ML Engineers
evidence.data_team_maturity: As part of the Data Analytics & AI team, you will supervise a team of Analytics Engineers, work closely with Data Engineers and AI/ML Engineers
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Multiple named, distinct data sub-teams (Analytics Engineers, Data Engineers, AI/ML Engineers) already exist within a Data Analytics & AI function at a $20B/15,000-employee enterprise, indicating an established, specialised team structure.
evidence.jd_authorship: Lead the design and development of interactive dashboards and reports using Power BI, ensuring a high level of user experience and functionality
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Some bullets name precise tools and concrete deliverables (Power BI dashboards, DAX, Microsoft Fabric, PySpark) while others are generic leadership boilerplate ("foster a culture of continuous improvement"), placing this in between hiring-manager precision and pure recruiter language.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Help spread the knowledge of data visualization to business users, fostering a data-literate culture across the organization
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on serving the data/analytics function itself (leading the Analytics Engineering team, defining data models with Data/AI engineers, governance standards) rather than any single external business function.
evidence.autonomy_level: Drive our data visualization and analytics strategies across the enterprise
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role sets enterprise-wide standards, governance, and strategy for analytics, and leads/supervises a team, placing it clearly in strategic/direction-setting territory.
evidence.ai_role: integrate predictive analytics, AI insights, and advanced analytical capabilities into business reporting where appropriate
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is expected to build reporting/data infrastructure that incorporates AI/ML outputs (working with AI/ML Engineers, integrating AI insights into dashboards), making AI downstream of the candidate's data work rather than a coding tool for the candidate.
evidence.testing_framing: Ensure data quality and governance in reporting environments, establishing standards for data visualization best practices and consistency
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality and governance appear as named responsibilities but are framed generically (standards/consistency) rather than a specific testing/data-contract practice the candidate personally owns and defines with concrete mechanisms.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Ensure that reporting solutions and related delivery processes are scalable, repeatable, secure, and measurable across people, processes, and technology
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Reliability/governance concerns (secure, repeatable, governed reporting) are present but secondary to the primary delivery/leadership framing, giving a moderate rather than high loss-aversion signal.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Stay updated on the latest trends, tools, and best practices... advocating for the adoption of modern techniques
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role operates within an existing, established analytics function and focuses on standardizing, governing, and modernizing current reporting practices rather than building from zero.
evidence.loss_aversion: "Ensure data quality and governance in reporting environments" reflects concern about unreliable/ungoverned reporting reaching business users, but this is secondary to the delivery/leadership framing.
